newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: BIL CEO sees 96 net up 9% at 3.1 bln Luxfr.
newsitem.headline: BIL CEO sees 96 net up 9% at 3.1 bln Luxfr.

text.p: Andre Roelants, the new chief executive oficer of Banque Internationale a Luxembourg SA (BIL) confirmed an earlier forecast that his bank's 1996 consolidated profit would rise about nine percent.

"At the start of the year I already said I expected to see our profit rise between eight and ten percent. A 3.1 billion franc profit would be a good approximation," Roelants told Reuters in an interview at a seminar about the Luxembourg financial market organised by Belgian financial daily L'Echo.
BIL is 52 percent owned by Belgian bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB).
Roelants also said that the outlook for 1997 was positive.

"We are on the same track as in 1996. Much will depend on market volatility. We have a good chance of staying on target. I do not rule out that we could see a repeat of the nine percent profit growth," Roelants said.

BIL is Luxembourg's largest bank in terms of balance sheet total. Total assets stood at 934.8 billion francs at the end of June 1996. Banque Generale du Luxembourg was a close second with total assets of 911.9 billion.
Full-year figures for 1996 are due in the coming weeks.
